AL-senate.statusNote: Open seat (Sen. Tuberville running for governor): Rep. Barry Moore (R) faces Birmingham attorney Everett Wess (D). Both won June 16 runoffs (Moore 55.8%, Wess 54.6%); independent educator Craig Jelks is also running.

candidates.name: Barry Moore
candidates.background: U.S. Representative since 2021 (AL-02, then AL-01 after redistricting); Army National Guard veteran and former waste-services small-business owner from Coffee County. Freedom Caucus conservative endorsed by President Trump. Won the June 16 Republican runoff for the open Senate seat with 55.8% over former Navy SEAL Jared Hudson.
priorities: Secure the border, 'zero tolerance for illegal immigration'
Back law enforcement and the pro-life movement

cost.label: Approach to affordability is to 'cut useless regulations, shrink the size of government, and restore freedom to our economy', touting tax cuts on tips, overtime and Social Security (campaign site)

climate.label: Voted yes on the Lower Energy Costs Act to expand domestic energy production and lower energy prices (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: 'Zero tolerance for illegal immigration'; voted for the bill providing $45 billion to ICE to deport illegal immigrants (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Backs cutting taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security plus small-business tax reductions through recent legislation; voted against the American Rescue Plan (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Opposes Common Core; 'parents' and 'local school boards' should control education, not the federal government (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: 'Violent criminals should be prosecuted to the fullest extent'; supports fully funding law enforcement (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Called overturning Roe 'a huge victory for the pro-life movement and the Constitution' (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted to object to certifying 2020 electoral votes on January 7, 2021 and posted false election-theft claims (Wikipedia)

health.label: Voted for the 2025 reconciliation law and touted its Medicaid restrictions, 'removing 1.4 million illegals, eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse' and barring Medicaid funding for transition procedures (Rep. Moore press release)

nullNotes.housing: checked Ballotpedia, Wikipedia and campaign issues page, nothing documented

controversies.label: Arrested in 2014 on felony perjury charges tied to a state corruption probe, acquitted at trial; later opposed the Congressional Gold Medal for January 6 Capitol police (Wikipedia)

education.label: Backs 'quality public education to equip our future leaders' (campaign site)

democracy.label: Pledges to 'advocate for voting rights' as a core campaign principle (campaign site)

candidates.name: Tommy Tuberville
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2021 and former college football head coach at Ole Miss, Auburn, Texas Tech and Cincinnati. Passed on Senate reelection to run for governor with President Trump's endorsement and won the May 19 Republican primary with 85% of the vote.
priorities: Secure the border and back Trump's deportation agenda
School choice, charter schools and local control of education
Lower taxes and less government spending

health.label: 'Obamacare must go. This failed experiment has led to higher costs, less quality care' (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: 'We must first secure our border'; 'fully support[s] President Trump's plan to build a wall' against 'illegal immigration that brings drugs, terrorists, and criminals' (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: 'Lower taxes create jobs and less spending reduces the size and scope of the federal government' (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Dismisses climate science, saying the global climate 'won't change enough in the next 400 years to affect anybody' (Wikipedia)

education.label: Supports 'school choice, charter schools, and improving our existing public schools'; says the best solutions 'come from the local level' (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Calls abortion 'this generation's holocaust' and pledges to 'fight to protect the sanctity of every human life'; blocked 451 military promotions over a Pentagon abortion-travel policy (Ballotpedia, Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Voted to object to certifying Arizona's and Pennsylvania's 2020 electoral votes (Wikipedia)

cost.label: Voted with 42 other Senate Republicans on Aug 7, 2022 to strip the $35 insulin copay cap for private insurance from the Inflation Reduction Act (Newsweek)

housing.label: One of five senators voting no on the ROAD to Housing Act, saying 'giving the federal government more control over housing is not the answer' and preferring market-driven solutions; also voted nay on the March 2026 housing supply bill (Time, Senate roll call 53)

safety.label: Pledged to the Alabama FOP to 'invest in training, equipment, and resources' so police are 'trained and empowered', and introduced the Empowering Law Enforcement Act (Tuberville Senate office)

controversies.label: Held up 451 senior military promotions for 10 months in 2023 over a Pentagon abortion-travel policy, leaving the Marine Corps without a confirmed commandant for the first time in two centuries (Wikipedia)
Violated the STOCK Act by failing to timely disclose roughly 132 stock trades in 2021; Washington Post reporting raised questions about his Florida residency (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Doug Jones
candidates.background: U.S. Senator from Alabama 2018 to 2021, the first Democrat to win an Alabama Senate seat in a quarter century; as U.S. Attorney he prosecuted the 1963 Birmingham church bombing case. Won the May 19 Democratic primary for governor with 78% of the vote.
priorities: Eliminate grocery, tip and overtime taxes to lower costs
Early voting and a citizen ballot initiative process

cost.label: Affordability agenda: eliminate grocery, tip and overtime taxes, raise worker wages statewide, invest in affordable childcare and paid family leave (Alabama Reflector)

health.label: 'Medicaid expansion is not a handout, it's a hand up'; Alabama lags 39 states that expanded (Alabama Reflector)

immigration.label: Voted for the McCain-Coons pathway to citizenship for Dreamers and against defunding sanctuary cities; agrees border security needs improvement but did not consider it a national emergency (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Mixed: opposed the TCJA as 'skewed to benefit the wealthy' yet has called for corporate tax reductions and has not called for tax increases (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Voted for the First Step Act to reduce recidivism and supports reversing mandatory three-strikes laws for nonviolent offenses (Wikipedia)

climate.label: 'I believe in science. The impact of unchecked fossil fuels on our planet and our health has not been in dispute for decades' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Advocates quality public education access regardless of socioeconomic status; championed HBCU funding increases (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: 'I will defend women's access to contraception and a woman's right to choose'; wants a constitutional amendment protecting contraception and IVF (Ballotpedia, Alabama Reflector)

democracy.label: Would implement early voting, create a citizen ballot initiative process and expand local authority (Alabama Reflector)
